question: Slovo „cosplay“, tedy převlékání za postavy z anime, her a filmů, vzniklo spojením dvou anglických slov. Kterých?
source_excerpt: The term was coined by Nobuyuki Takahashi of Studio Hard in an article for the Japanese magazine My Anime in June 1983.

extra.why_interesting: Players hear 'cosplay' at every Czech convention and assume it is a plain English word or some exotic Japanese term. In fact a Japanese journalist made it up by blending two English words, so the word travelled from America through Japan before reaching Brno. Most players can work out the two halves themselves.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms cosplay is a Japanese blend of the English words 'costume' and 'play'; the 1983/1984 dating dispute doesn't affect the answer.

explanation: Slovo vymyslel v roce 1984 japonský novinář Nobuyuki Takahashi poté, co viděl převlečené fanoušky na sci-fi setkání v Los Angeles. Anglické slovo tedy stvořil Japonec a do Česka k nám dorazilo z Japonska.

question: Ve kterém českém městě se každoročně koná Animefest, největší festival anime a japonské popkultury v Česku, kam se sjíždějí tisíce fanoušků v kostýmech?
source_excerpt: Animefest 2026 ran May 22–24, 2026, at the Brno Exhibition Centre

extra.why_interesting: Many players expect a big pop-culture event to take place in Prague by default. The biggest Czech anime festival is actually a Brno tradition. A player who has seen the crowds of costumed fans in Moravia gets it right away, and others can reach it by doubting the obvious Prague guess.
extra.verification_notes: Animefest is held annually in Brno; the 2026 edition took place at the Brno Exhibition Centre, per the official site https://www.animefest.cz/en/Rocnik/Index/2026.

explanation: Animefest se v Brně koná už od roku 2004. Kdo tam ten víkend přijede, potká v ulicích Moravy samurajské meče a růžové paruky.
